steps: It is week twenty-seven, and there will be no big-bang release. Before any traffic moves, you arm the rollback gate: revert if accuracy drops more than two points, or hallucination rises one point, from a ninety-five point eight percent baseline.
In stage one, the traffic splitter routes the hybrid retrieval release to five percent of clinicians, for forty-eight hours.
After forty-eight hours, the gate checks the canary: ninety-six point two percent accuracy and one point eight percent hallucination. It passes, so the canary widens to twenty-five percent.
Stage two passes too, at ninety-six point one percent and one point nine percent, so the gate widens the canary to fifty percent for twenty-four hours.
Now at stage three, accuracy falls to ninety-three point two percent, a two point six point drop. That is over the two point limit, so the threshold is breached.
Rollback is automatic. The gate reverts all traffic to the baseline and pages the on-call engineer with an accuracy regression alert.

Finally, half the clinicians never saw the regression. On-call follows the runbook and escalates, and you trace the drop to rare claim types, then refine the re-ranker and re-test. The damage was contained.
